page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.large is an entry-level, general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. This yields a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance metrics indicate that the ecs.mn4.large is positioned for low-intensity workloads. In stress-ng benchmarks, the instance achieved a single-core CPU score of 1090.78 and a multi-core score of 2067.18, placing its compute capabilities in the lower tier. Memory bandwidth tests show 158.75 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, which drops to 16.93 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 13.99 GB/sec for large-block writes. Geekbench testing aligns with these results, yielding a single-core score of 939.0 and a multi-core score of 1598.0, with software compilation and image processing tasks also registering in the lower performance brackets.

The shared CPU allocation model represents a key architectural tradeoff, trading dedicated compute performance for qualitative cost efficiency. This resource density makes the instance a budget-conscious option for workloads that do not require sustained high CPU utilization. For example, static web serving throughput reached 2.32 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations achieved 2.58 million operations per second, demonstrating viability for lightweight application hosting.

Given these specifications and benchmark results, the ecs.mn4.large is best suited for basic general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include lightweight web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, basic text processing, and low-traffic database operations that do not demand high-speed local storage or high network throughput.
